title: Hosted API enterprise intake: SLA-aware scoring and onboarding checklist for chat/streaming/tool-calls
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a repeatable, SLA-aware scoring rubric and onboarding checklist for enterprise Hosted API feature requests that involve chat streaming, tool/function calls, or structured outputs. The outcome should be a single-page scorer PMs can run during intake to produce a priority band, a required artifact checklist for engineering/security, and a recommended rollout path (canary, A/B, full rollout). This ticket does not change API surface; it standardizes triage and handoff to ENG and Design.
scoring_rubric: Customer size weight: 0-5 (5 = Fortune 100; 1 = small SaaS) - guides SLA tier and priority
Usage profile weight: 0-5 (streaming sessions per minute, tokens/sec) - maps to Dedicated vs Hosted routing
Data sensitivity weight: 0-5 (PII/regulatory) - flags Private/VPC requirement and KMS needs
Business criticality weight: 0-5 (blocking user flow, revenue impact) - escalates to P0/P1
Operational complexity weight: 0-5 (tool chains, multi-turn tool-calls, long-running streams) - flags engineering effort and observability needs
Compatibility risk weight: 0-3 (requires structured outputs / function calling changes) - may require SDK contract reviews
Total score bands: 0-6 = Low (Backlog), 7-12 = Medium (Planned), 13-20 = High (Planned/In Progress + Sales/CS alignment)
Auto-actions: scores >=15 require security_review_required=true and dedicated onboarding sync with Solutions Eng
onboarding_checklist: Required customer artifacts: sample prompt corpus, expected success criteria, target SLAs (p95 latency, concurrency) (customer-provided or from Sales)
Security artifacts: data classification, retention requirements, KMS/HSM preferences, any export controls
Engineering intake: expected QPS, tokens/sec, typical sequence length, KV cache savings estimate
Design/UX: sample UI flows for streaming and tool calls, example structured JSON schemas for outputs
Monitoring: define key metrics (latency p50/p95/p99, error rate, token cost delta) and set initial alert thresholds
Rollout plan: suggested path (alpha internal -> customer canary -> 10% tenant A/B -> ramp) and rollback criteria
Acceptance criteria: end-to-end test vector set with pass/fail thresholds and manual sign-off owners (PM/ENG/SEC/CS)
Docs/SDK: callouts required for SDKs (streaming hooks, function-call schema), sample snippets for customers
acceptance_criteria: Single-page scorer template exists in Confluence and can be completed in <15 minutes
Checklist items map to concrete artifacts; missing artifacts cause auto-assign to Solutions Eng owner
Triage outputs (score and recommended path) deterministically map to route: hosted standard / hosted priority / dedicated / private
Security gate defined: any intake with data sensitivity >=3 triggers security_review_required=true and requires Security review within 3 working days
PM + ENG runbook created for at least two representative customer requests and validated in an intake dry-run
Console changes required for tenant routing (if any) are captured as follow-up ENG tickets
notes: Decision: keep scoring lightweight; avoid hard thresholds that block sales. Scoring produces recommendation, approvals still required for P0/P1
Trade-off: tighter security gating increases time-to-onboard but reduces rework for Private deployments. Chosen balance: require security review only for sensitivity >=3 or scores >=15
Related artifacts: PRD draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/hosted-api/sla-aware-intake (internal), Intake examples slide deck: drive.google.com/drive/folders/example-intake
Referenced tickets: ENG-1842 (autoscaler capacity telemetry), PM-4923 (hosted API intake framework) - intake should align to those signals
Ask for ENG: ability to export QPS and tokens/s forecasts from routing service to intake form for better score accuracy
